title: App C and tier self-check
intro: Inheritance, which sections carry extra controls, and what you must not decide alone.

choices: Tier 3 includes every Tier 2 Appendix C control, plus the Tier 3-only rows.
Tier 3 replaces Tier 2 and drops the Tier 2 rows.
Tier 1 includes Appendix C.
Pick either Tier 2 or Tier 3 rows, not both.
questions.rationale: G3 Appendix C says the Tier 2 controls shall also be adopted by Tier 3 systems.

questions.prompt: Which areas add Tier 3-only organisation, risk, and training controls?
choices: §12 only.
§3 normative references.
None. Appendix C is only about passwords.
questions.rationale: Steering committee and certification are §5. Risk registers are §7. Structured training is §9. They are Tier 3 rows. Other sections still have Tier 2 rows that Tier 3 inherits.

questions.prompt: The privileged-account audit and privileged MFA rules are:
choices: Tier 2 controls, so Tier 3 takes them too.
Tier 3 only, so a Tier 2 system can skip them.
Optional for Internet-facing systems.
Replaced by a longer screensaver.
questions.rationale: They sit in the Tier 2 column of App C §11. Empty Tier 3 cells in that row do not cancel them.

questions.prompt: An Internet-facing Tier 2 system needs penetration testing:
choices: At least once a year, and penetration testing is also part of the security risk assessment for Tier 2.
Never.
Only after a redesign of the logo.
Only if the system is also Tier 3.
questions.rationale: App C §20: pen-test in the SRA for Tier 2, and at least yearly for Internet-facing Tier 2. Tier 3 has a further annual SRA package.

questions.prompt: A Tier 3 security risk assessment under App C includes:
choices: At least an annual assessment, with vulnerability scanning, an independent accredited penetration test, and configuration and source review, endorsed by the DITSO.
A verbal “looks fine”.
A scan once per decade.
A test done only by the developer who wrote the code, with no independence.
questions.rationale: That is the Tier 3 compliance row. Always read the current Appendix C wording before you quote a deadline in a paper.

questions.prompt: You think a system might be Tier 2. What do you do?
choices: Propose the tier with impact, interdependency, and essential-service notes, then confirm with the Information Owner or DITSO unit.
Stamp Tier 3 on the architecture slide yourself.
Ignore Appendix C until an audit.
Treat the hub checkbox as the official classification.
questions.rationale: Classification is a management act under §7. This hub is a learning aid, not the decision.

questions.prompt: Which statement about an empty Tier 2 cell is right?
choices: That area has no extra Tier 2 control in Appendix C. Baseline S17/G3 still applies. Tier 3-only rows do not erase Tier 2 rows elsewhere.
An empty cell means the whole section is optional.
An empty cell means you can skip Shall.
An empty cell downgrades the system to Tier 1.
questions.rationale: Read the matrix by row. Inheritance is across the Tier 2 column, not cancelled by a dash in one cell.
